version.changelog:
constraint-engine 1.3.0

- Data handling model updated: now operates within the agent’s trust boundary, using the agent’s configured model for constraint checking/generation (no external calls).
- Removed: `disable-model-invocation` flag and related instruction-only messaging.
- Tags updated for clarity and broader discoverability.
- Documentation clarified for new agent-centric operation and security boundaries.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are consistent with its described purpose (generating and enforcing constraints from observed failures); it asks for no credentials, has no install step, and only reads/writes within the agent workspace/configs it declares.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (constraint generation, enforcement, lifecycle) align with the declared needs: configuration files and a workspace for outputs. The README references an optional dependency (failure-memory) for observations which is coherent with generating constraints from past failures.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to check actions against constraints, generate constraints from observations, manage lifecycle, and write results to output/constraints/. It does not request unrelated system-wide data or credentials. It relies on the agent's model and configured failure-memory data — consistent with its purpose. The docs do allow autonomous pre-action triggers, which is expected for an enforcement skill.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no external binaries; lowest-risk install model. It suggests optional openclaw install commands for complementary skills but does not fetch arbitrary code or external archives itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables or secrets are declared. Declared config paths (.openclaw/constraint-engine.yaml and .claude/constraint-engine.yaml) are proportional to a configurable enforcement skill. No unrelated credentials or high-privilege paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (good). The skill can be invoked autonomously (platform default) and can trigger pre-action checks; this is expected for a guardrail. Users should note that it can block or alter agent actions when triggered, but the skill does not request elevated system-wide persistence or to modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally coherent and doesn't ask for secrets, but review the two declared config files before enabling it (.openclaw/constraint-engine.yaml and .claude/constraint-engine.yaml) so you know what thresholds and behaviors it will enforce. Note that it can run pre-action checks and temporarily override or block agent actions; test it in a safe workspace first, and install the optional failure-memory dependency only if you trust its source. If you want stricter control, require manual invocation instead of allowing automatic pre-action triggers.
